title: centaurea iberica subsp. holzmanniana
intro: Centaurea iberica subsp. holzmanniana, commonly known as Holzmann's knapweed, is a plant species belonging to the family Asteraceae. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine, particularly in the Caucasus region, to treat various health issues. The plant has been reported to possess several health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which may help alleviate symptoms associated with respiratory and gastrointestinal disorders. The bioactive constituents of Centaurea iberica subsp. holzmanniana include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to be responsible for its therapeutic actions.
